# Point-to-Gaussian Generation

Also called: DiffGS Point-to-Gaussian, Point Cloud to Gaussian Generation

## Overview
Point-to-Gaussian Generation synthesizes [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) attributes directly from 3D point cloud geometry, bridging sparse geometric inputs and dense radiance field representations [S1]. Unlike the parent [Point Cloud to Gaussian Converter](1788-point-cloud-to-gaussian-converter.md), which uses deterministic proximity-based variance functions, this method employs a trained generative model to predict Gaussian attributes from geometry alone [S1].

## How it works
**Inputs:** A 3D point cloud $P = \{p_i\}_{i=1}^N$ [S1].
**Outputs:** A set of Gaussian attributes $\{G_j\}$ defining the [3DGS representation](#12855-gaussian-representation-and-truncation.md), including mean, covariance, color, and opacity [S1].
**Data Structures:** The method uses a Gaussian Variational Autoencoder (VAE) trained with 3D point clouds as inputs instead of 3DGS with attributes [S1]. The broader DiffGS framework also employs a [latent diffusion model](#14900-latent-diffusion-models-ldm.md) to generate functions modeling Gaussian probabilities, colors, and transforms [S1]. Implementation details for data preparation and network architecture are deferred to the source appendix [S1].
**Steps:**
1. **Input Preparation:** The 3D point cloud is processed as the input tensor for the generative model [S1].
2. **Model Inference:** The trained Gaussian VAE processes the point cloud to predict attributes directly from geometry, bypassing standard 3DGS [rasterization-based optimization](#3378-snugbox.md) [S1].
3. **Attribute Generation:** The model outputs the Gaussian attributes [S1].
4. **Octree-Guided Extraction:** An octree-guided extraction algorithm generates 3DGS with an arbitrary number of Gaussians [S1].
**Formulas:** Not given in the sources.
**Parameters:**
- **Training Data:** ShapeNet (chair and airplane classes) and DeepFashion3D (real-captured 3D dataset with complex textures) [S1].
- **Evaluation Metrics:** PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS are used to evaluate the reconstructed 3DGS quality [S1].
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
- Specific hyperparameters for the VAE/diffusion model (e.g., latent dimension, diffusion steps) are not detailed in the main text and require reference to the source's appendix [S1].
- Performance on extremely sparse point clouds is not evaluated in the sources [G].

## Subtopics

### Octree-Guided Extraction
An algorithm used by DiffGS to generate 3DGS with an arbitrary number of Gaussians [S1].

### LIV-GaussMap
Initializes Gaussians with a LiDAR point cloud for easier initialization and builds an optimizable size-adaptive voxel grid for the [global map](#16569-rnr-map-data-structure.md) [S2, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
- **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
- **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
- **Performance:** Visual results demonstrate accurate prediction of Gaussian attributes for 3D point clouds across tested datasets (ShapeNet, DeepFashion3D) [S1]. The method produces visual-appealing 3DGS generations given only 3D point cloud geometries [S1].
- **Strengths:** Bridges easily accessible point clouds with powerful 3DGS representations; enables content generation by connecting geometry to appearance [S1].
- **Limitations:** Requires a pre-trained generative model; specific implementation details (data preparation, network architecture) are deferred to the appendix [S1].

## Background
The method was introduced in the DiffGS ([Functional Gaussian Splatting](#15572-functional-gaussian-splatting-representation.md) Diffusion) paper [S1]. It addresses the challenge of generating 3DGS from point clouds, a task vital for connecting sparse geometric data with dense radiance field representations [S1]. The work builds on previous efforts in [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) completion and [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md) for 3D generation [S1].
